newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor may boost Yankee issue to $300 mln.
newsitem.headline: Koor may boost Yankee issue to $300 mln.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries is considering increasing its planned Yankee bond offering to $300 million from $200 million, a spokesman said on Sunday.
The issue, the first overseas debt offering by an Israeli private sector company, is scheduled for end-July or early August. A roadshow is scheduled to start in mid-July, the spokesman told Reuters.
The decision came after Koor CEO Benjamin Gaon met with underwriters Goldman Sachs, Salomon Brothers and Lehman Brothers last week.

Koor, Israel's largest holding company, has said the proceeds would be used mainly to acquire overseas companies in its core businesses -- telecommunications, electronics, chemicals and infrastructure.
Representatives of Standard and Poor's and Moody's will be meeting with Koor management this week to assign Koor its first-ever rating.
